title: Classification
body:
[[Binary Classification]]
[[Confusion Matrix]]

---

Predict which of a **finite, unordered** set of labels an input belongs to. That is the whole
definition, and both adjectives do work: finite rules out regression, unordered means the labels
carry no arithmetic, so predicting "cat" when the answer is "dog" is not more or less wrong than
predicting "bird".

| | Classification | Regression |
|---|---|---|
| Output | a label from a finite set | a number |
| Model outputs | a [[Probability Distribution]] over labels | the value itself |
| Typical loss | [[Cross-Entropy Loss]], [[Log Loss]] | squared error, a [[Vector Norm]] |
| [[Output Layer]] | [[Sigmoid]] or softmax | no activation |
| Judged by | [[Confusion Matrix]] rates | residual size |
| Simplest example | [[Logistic Regression]] | [[Linear Regression]] |

**A classifier does not output a label, it outputs probabilities.** The label comes from applying a
threshold afterward, and that threshold is a separate decision with its own costs, which is why the
[[Sensitivity]] / [[Specificity]] trade-off exists at all. Keeping the two steps distinct is the
thing to hold onto: the model is fitted once, the threshold can be moved afterward without
retraining.

## The shape of the job

1. **Split the data**, using [[Stratification]] so the test set is honest.
2. **Fit a model** ([[Logistic Regression]], a [[Neural Network]], a decision tree) by minimising
   [[Cross-Entropy Loss]] with [[Gradient Descent]].
3. **Evaluate** with a [[Confusion Matrix]] on data the model has not seen, and report per-class
   rates rather than accuracy.

Step 3 is where most of the marks are, because it is where the reasoning is. The
[[MACHINE LEARNING]] parent's model / loss / optimiser table covers step 2.

**Supervised**, meaning every training example comes with its true label. The unsupervised
counterpart is clustering, which groups without labels and cannot be scored this way;
[[Principal Component Analysis]] is the unsupervised method the vault does have a note for.
